sources.title: Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) - Seattle
sources.note: Defines end-to-end ownership from discovery and scoping through build, rollout, adoption, and reusable field learning.

sources.title: OpenAI careers search: forward deployed
sources.note: Snapshot showed 22 matching roles across general, healthcare, government, security, software engineering, deployment leadership, and multiple regions. This is not a labor-market census.

sources.title: Forward Deployed Engineer
sources.note: Calls for production customer artifacts including MCP servers, sub-agents, and agent skills, alongside evals and production LLM delivery.

sources.title: Forward Deployed Engineer, GenAI
sources.note: Emphasizes high-quality data infrastructure, large-scale processing, customer-specific systems, full-stack delivery, and rapid experimentation.

sources.title: Forward-Deployed Engineer
sources.note: Separates AI-builder and Next.js-focused profiles while requiring embedded delivery, live code, production agents, MCP, and customer knowledge transfer.

sources.title: Forward Deployed Engineer
sources.note: Highlights the production reliability cliff, full Agent Development Life Cycle, golden datasets, regressions, tracing, and judgment about whether a workflow needs an agent.

sources.title: Architecture center overview
sources.note: Describes FDE as a human feedback mechanism that gets close to hard missions, synthesizes field learning, and ships product features.

sources.title: AI FDE overview
sources.note: Shows an AI-assisted FDE model with controlled context, permission-respecting tools, closed-loop actions, previews, CI validation, and reviewed changes.

sources.title: The 2026-07-28 Specification
sources.note: Current release notes cover stateless operation, routing headers, cacheable lists, authorization hardening, and the Tasks extension.

sources.title: Agent2Agent Protocol Specification
sources.note: Defines messages, tasks, streaming updates, subscriptions, authorization scoping, and push notifications for disconnected or long-running work.

sources.title: Effective context engineering for AI agents
sources.note: Frames context as a managed, scarce resource and argues for clear prompts, minimal non-overlapping tools, canonical examples, and just-in-time retrieval.

sources.title: Equipping agents for the real world with Agent Skills
sources.note: Explains progressive disclosure through skill metadata, instructions, references, and deterministic scripts, with evaluation-first development.

sources.title: Generative AI semantic conventions
sources.note: Defines GenAI telemetry attributes and explicitly warns that prompts, retrieval queries, tool arguments, and outputs can contain sensitive information.

sources.title: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications
sources.note: Provides an agent-specific risk taxonomy spanning goal hijack, tool misuse, identity abuse, supply chain, code execution, memory poisoning, inter-agent communication, and cascading failures.

sources.title: AI Risk Management Framework: Generative AI Profile
sources.note: Cross-sector companion to the NIST AI RMF for incorporating trustworthiness into GenAI design, development, use, and evaluation.

sources.title: Durable Execution Solutions
sources.note: Illustrates durable workflow state, retries, task queues, signals, timers, human intervention, and resumption after infrastructure failure. Vendor claims are treated as architectural examples, not neutral benchmarks.
